consumer_separation.effect: Existing point becomes eligible for native input subject to mode, distance and input gates.

consumer_separation.producer: status==1 selects the open portal effect

consumer_separation.consumer: No gate-mesh state adapter is established by the selected point consumer.
consumer_separation.producer: Requires explicit selected asset/controller integration if a solid gate is authored.
consumer_separation.effect: Server MEF development/integration requirement for that chosen experience.

consumer_separation.consumer: Existing Server static BND plus flag-barrier overlay
consumer_separation.producer: Committed instance flags, not Client portal appearance
consumer_separation.effect: Server movement/path/projectile/interaction collision policy as documented in FLAG-BARRIERS.md.

contracts.player_result: Enter the selected map at a valid authored spawn.
contracts.current_mef: Node map/spawn and exit destination are authored data. MapID joins the selected _MapList row and BOUND member.
contracts.client_reuse: Existing map/world setup and point input consumers.
contracts.predicate: 0<=x<worldWidth, 0<=y<worldHeight; floor(x*gridWidth/worldWidth), floor(y*gridHeight/worldHeight); nonzero layer 0 OR layer 1 is blocked under the current Server policy.
contracts.remaining: MapID assignment alone is not map-ready. Owner, point snapshot, current node, content revision and scene completion must belong to the same installed generation.

contracts.player_result: See an exit unlock and press Z at the intended destination.
contracts.current_mef: One main exit plus up to seven alternatives; exact category/key and authored action/target node.
contracts.client_reuse: 0027 creates the complete point set; 0048 or the existing Lua setter changes an installed point; 001C returns category/key.
contracts.predicate: Category 0 native distance is strictly less than 0.8*wireRadius. The Server authored radius is inclusive and does not automatically receive that scaling.
contracts.remaining: A full 0027 replaces the set and local status. Restore all surviving exits/markers/manual points after a scene; do not append one point at a time or treat 003F as proof of setter success.

contracts.player_result: Choose one branch without accidentally taking the other.
contracts.current_mef: The Server resolves the exact provided key, or its documented fallback chooses nearest in-range then smallest key on a tie. Only OpenExitKeys authorize a transfer.
contracts.client_reuse: Native nearest eligible point and mode/input gates; the Server fallback tie rule is not asserted as a native tie rule.
contracts.predicate: Clear aggregate group AND exit-specific requiredFlags AND optional current activationRegion; once qualified, the exit latches open.
contracts.remaining: A branch chart being acyclic does not prove physical access or safe visible placement. Preserve the selected exit key/position through the transition transaction.

contracts.player_result: Press Z once at a mechanism to satisfy the configured condition.
contracts.current_mef: CheckpointInteracted, category 1/key, region, optional prior flags and group-clear requirement. A successful interaction sets a fixed instance flag and disables that point.
contracts.client_reuse: Existing category-1 input emits 001C in the established ordinary-mode path; no new gameplay opcode.
contracts.predicate: Native distance <wireRadius; Server region distance<=radius plus current instance/node, owned living actor and enabled state. An optional distinct category-0 marker remains disabled.
contracts.remaining: Category 1 has no proven category-0-like visual. A lever/chest/breakable model and animation require a chosen presentation adapter; the point is not itself a save policy.

contracts.player_result: Entering the authored circle can raise a flag or permit a wave/exit.
contracts.current_mef: Circle center/radius; signal flags and current-position gates have different latching behavior.
contracts.client_reuse: Visual cues may use supported native presentation, but no generic local region-fact-to-authoritative-event bridge is established by the point evidence.
contracts.predicate: Inclusive circle. A wave activationRegion requires the current observed position at evaluation; entering earlier then leaving is not enough. RegionEntered raises its once-only instance flag when observed inside.
contracts.remaining: No swept-segment/crossing trigger is promised. Polygon, height, moving regions and any/all-party occupancy need explicit MEF schema and predicate semantics if requested.

contracts.player_result: Stay inside a circle continuously for the authored time to open the exit.
contracts.current_mef: RegionHeld with hold duration 0.25..3600 seconds. The Q119 node-4 candidate uses radius 2 and 2.5 seconds.
contracts.client_reuse: Optional local countdown/indicator presentation after a properly bound instruction; completion remains the configured Server MEF fact.
contracts.predicate: First inside observation starts; observed movement or skill displacement outside resets; downed and mainline-clear commit reset incomplete hold; mainline scene time is excluded; completed flag remains for the instance.
contracts.remaining: No current generic region/countdown visualization binding is established by this audit. Match visible countdown to this exact clock and reset semantics, not a generic NodeDelay timer.

contracts.player_result: Remaining in a trap circle causes periodic damage; leaving or disabling it stops the countdown.
contracts.current_mef: Up to 16 circular hazards/node, damage 1..500, interval 0.25..3600 seconds, optional disabledByFlag; Q119 candidate has radius 3, 25 damage per second, disabled by a 14-second node flag.
contracts.client_reuse: Existing health/hurt/death presentation; local warning effects can be added through a selected supported presentation route.
contracts.predicate: Start at first observed inside; full interval before first damage; observed outside resets; one tick maximum per late update; overlapping hazards have independent timers; stop on disable, aggregate clear or map change; pending waves keep the battle active.
contracts.remaining: The selected content has no established matching visible trap area/countdown adapter. Fixed damage has no attacker and is not automatically the ordinary enemy hit/dodge/block policy.

contracts.player_result: A configured local obstruction disappears when its flag is committed.
contracts.current_mef: Up to 16 axis-aligned rectangles/node; opensWithFlag; optional portal-style marker.
contracts.client_reuse: Marker point appearance can reuse category 0; it is separate from Server blockage.
contracts.predicate: Cell-center test with minX/minY inclusive and maxX/maxY exclusive. A cell covered by several closed barriers remains blocked until every covering barrier opens. Base BND walls remain; opening invalidates obsolete detour paths.
contracts.remaining: All three present Q119 barrier candidates allow a static route around the rectangle. They are local obstacles plus a conditional exit. A physically sealed gate requires a choke-point cut and independent Client mesh/collision integration.

contracts.player_result: A guard patrols, pursues within its home range, and returns without walking through static walls.
contracts.current_mef: One to sixteen waypoints; every segment, including the return, has length >0 and <=256; profile aggroRange and spawn-centered leashRadius; every segment is checked.
contracts.client_reuse: Existing native movement/animation handling. This audit does not claim a new collision bypass or new savings for presentation already performed locally.
contracts.predicate: Aggro is measured from current monster position; leash from spawn. Leaving leash cancels pending hit and returns home preserving HP/cooldown. Bounded four-neighbor search: <=4096 cells and <=1 monster search/battle update; chase replan after >=0.5 seconds and target movement >=2.
contracts.remaining: Selected BND policy covers static terrain; moving obstacles, party blocking, moving-platform connectivity and actor-width clearance require explicit extensions. Actual Client/Server position alignment remains a play gate.

contracts.player_result: A previous room's delayed switch cannot operate the new room's similarly numbered point.
contracts.current_mef: Bind authored point declarations and rule outputs to the current instance, node and selected content revision. Rebuild the full point snapshot after the chosen scene lifecycle.
contracts.client_reuse: The real wire contains category/key, not a map/run token. Same-map reinstallation and point replacement are lifetime changes even if MapID stays equal.
contracts.predicate: Generation change invalidates queued deltas and obsolete region/hazard/patrol work before installing the new point set. 0027 is replacement, not additive; setter success is not separately acknowledged.
contracts.remaining: The release adapter must enforce its own current-generation dispatch binding; do not invent a wire field or assume changing field automatically cancels an older Lua coroutine.

optimization_proposals.proposal: Cache immutable geometry by BND decoded hash plus policy version while retaining MapID and per-instance overlay identity.
optimization_proposals.measurable_target: This corpus resolves 118 MapIDs to 74 BND members. A cold per-MapID decoder can avoid 44 duplicate decodes; this is a decode-count comparison, not a measured CPU percentage.
optimization_proposals.preserve: Separate per-instance barrier states and generation; no mutation of the shared base grid.

optimization_proposals.proposal: Compile flag-to-dependent-exits/barriers/interactions and region-to-dependent-rules indices at load time.
optimization_proposals.measurable_target: Count rules evaluated per accepted position/flag event and number of actual changed outputs; unchanged flags must not cause duplicate 0048 or collision rebuild.
optimization_proposals.preserve: Observe movement/displacement exits promptly so hold/hazard reset semantics stay exact; no invented swept-crossing trigger.

optimization_proposals.proposal: Use one complete point snapshot for installation/rebuild and only changed point deltas between replacements.
optimization_proposals.measurable_target: Count 0027 replacements, rows, 0048 changes, bytes and point-count retention after the scene. A missing point or a scene rebuild still requires the full selected set.
optimization_proposals.preserve: Local setter changes do not survive a later replacement unless represented by the new authoritative snapshot; generation binds every queued operation.

optimization_proposals.proposal: Keep hazard and hold deadlines in indexed schedules with state-change cancellation; use Client effects for presentation where the selected profile permits.
optimization_proposals.measurable_target: Count active timer entries, due callbacks and region predicates per update for identical content; compare normal completion and reset points.
optimization_proposals.preserve: No catch-up hazard burst, no first-tick acceleration, no mainline-scene hold time, and no replacement of clear/hold facts by an arbitrary wait.

optimization_proposals.proposal: Prevalidate patrol loops and reuse bounded paths until target movement or affected obstacle generation invalidates them.
optimization_proposals.measurable_target: Count BFS starts, expanded cells, cache reuse, blocked-stop messages and successful resumes. Retain <=4096-cell and <=1-search-per-update bounds unless explicitly redesigned.
optimization_proposals.preserve: Leash origin, current-position aggro, hit line-of-sight, HP/cooldown preservation, and old-route invalidation on barrier change.

optimization_proposals.proposal: Choose local finite MEF presentation only for a real multi-step sequence and its compatible control/lifecycle profile.
optimization_proposals.measurable_target: Compare removed Server presentation timers and step dispatches against the actual selector/completion traffic. A single 0048 may be cheaper than starting a finite scene.
optimization_proposals.preserve: Already-native movement/point selection is not a new saving; authoritative spatial facts, exit conditions and saves remain in the shared MEF/adapter system.
